doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Staying home, image and being a woman leader
title: John Levy and his roster of top acts
summary: She explains John Levy managed Wes Montgomery, Nancy Wilson, Joe Williams and Cannonball and cared for her.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: What was it like to go from a large label, for that time anyway, like Mercury, to an independent label like Perception Records? Clearly, the budget, the personnel were not, you know, the kind of personnel you were able to choose with Mercury and have them paid for is probably not the case. There were budgetary restraints that probably didn‘t make that possible with Perception.
Well, darling, you know what? I didn‘t realize anything, because I had a man named John Levy. You know who he is?
I know the name very well, but I don‘t know exactly why. I know he‘s an agent.
That‘s right. At that time, John Levy had, oh, good lord, he had all the top acts. He had Wes Montgomery. Well, he‘s had Nancy Wilson and Joe Williams for fifty years.
